title: Our Lady of Lourdes (11 February)
hook: the World Day of the Sick

segments.voice: Yesterday, Candlemas: Simeon, an old man holding a baby, singing that he could go in peace. Your line was a light to the nations. Who got a little of your light? Day six hundred fifty.

Stand in the great square at Lourdes, in the south of France, on a summer evening, and watch the candlelight procession form. Thousands of people singing, each with a candle in a paper shield. And at the very front, not bishops, not dignitaries: people in wheelchairs and on rolling stretchers, pushed by volunteers who pay their own way to come and do it. At Lourdes the order of things is turned around. The ones the rest of the world sends to the back are put first. It all started with a poor, sick girl gathering firewood.
screen: `A SQUARE FULL OF CANDLES.` → `WHEELCHAIRS AT THE FRONT.` → `A GIRL GATHERING FIREWOOD.`

segments.voice: Her name was Bernadette Soubirous. She was fourteen, often sick with asthma, barely schooled, and her family was so poor they lived in a single room that had once been the town jail. On February 11, 1858, she went with her sister and a friend to gather wood near a grotto by the river, called Massabielle. There, she said, she saw a young lady dressed in white, with a blue sash and a rosary. Over the next months Bernadette reported eighteen visits. The lady asked for prayer and penance for sinners, and for a chapel. Once she told Bernadette to dig in the mud at the back of the grotto; a trickle came up, and it became the spring that still flows there. On March 25, when Bernadette asked her name, the lady answered in the local dialect, in words that are usually given as: I am the Immaculate Conception. Bernadette didn't know what the phrase meant. The parish priest, who had been skeptical, did. Pope Pius IX had defined that teaching only four years earlier. The bishop approved the apparitions in 1862. Bernadette herself never stayed for the crowds. She became a nun, lived quietly, and died at thirty-five, still often sick. Millions now come to Lourdes, and the Church has formally recognized around seventy healings as miraculous, after long medical review. Most pilgrims go home unhealed, and many say they came home changed anyway. In 1992 Pope John Paul II, himself slowed by illness, made February 11 the World Day of the Sick.
screen: `BERNADETTE, FOURTEEN, POOR.` · `A LADY AT MASSABIELLE.` · `DIG HERE: A SPRING.` · `I AM THE IMMACULATE CONCEPTION.` · then, large: `THE SICK COME FIRST.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: bring someone sick to mind and plan to reach them. Sit, and breathe. Picture one person who is ill right now: in a hospital, in a care home, at home with something long and tiring. Picture their room. What would it mean to them to hear from you? Decide: a visit, a call, a card, a meal at the door. Pick a time. If you pray, you can ask Our Lady of Lourdes to be with them. If you don't, simply hold them in your attention. The bell holds the time.
Our Lady of Lourdes. Mary as she appeared, Catholics believe, to Bernadette Soubirous in 1858; kept on February 11, the World Day of the Sick. Today's word.
Your line: the sick come first. Today, make the visit or the call before anything optional on your list. Day six hundred fifty.

howItsDone: On February 11 Catholics keep the memorial of Our Lady of Lourdes and the World Day of the Sick; many parishes offer the Anointing of the Sick, and Lourdes itself welcomes millions of pilgrims each year.

fork.reveal: she dug, and people laughed at her muddy face. the trickle became the spring that still flows at Lourdes.

trapdoor: what you thought: Lourdes is a place for miracle cures.
what it means: a shrine where a poor sick girl saw Mary, and where the sick are put first.
what a scholar hears: eighteen reported apparitions in 1858; 'I am the Immaculate Conception' came four years after the 1854 definition, and the Lourdes Medical Bureau reviews claimed cures.
